title: Olive oil biscotti
subtitle: twice-baked Italian biscuits made with olive oil and almonds
excerpt: Biscotti made with olive oil instead of butter have a slightly lighter, crispier texture and a subtle fruitiness from the oil. They are baked twice: first as a log until firm, then sliced and returned to the oven to dry out to a complete crunch. The slices can be stored for up to a month and are excellent with coffee or dessert wine.
sourceNotes: Biscotti (twice-baked Italian biscuits) have roots in the cantucci tradition of Tuscany; olive oil versions documented in Italian home-baking from at least the early twentieth century.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian twice-baked biscuits: the dough is shaped into a log and baked once, then sliced and returned to the oven to dry out. The result is very crisp and hard, suitable for dipping in coffee or vin santo.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 4 weeks at room temperature.
recipe.temperatureNote: 170°C fan / 190°C conventional / gas 5 for first bake; 150°C fan / 170°C conventional / gas 3 for second bake

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 170°C fan for first bake; 150°C fan for second bake

content.text: Olive oil biscotti use extra virgin olive oil in place of butter, which gives a less rich but crispier result. These are
so very dry and hard: they are designed for dipping, not eating dry. Use a mild extra virgin olive oil rather than a very peppery or grassy one, which can give a slightly bitter biscotti.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Line a large baking tray with baking parchment.
Whisk together the eggs, olive oil, vanilla extract, and lemon zest in a large bowl. Add the flour, caster sugar, baking powder, and salt and mix to a stiff dough. Fold in the toasted almonds.
Divide the dough into two equal portions. Shape each into a log about 28 cm long and 6 cm wide on the prepared tray, leaving space between them. Wet hands make this easier.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until pale golden and firm to the touch. Remove from the oven and leave to cool on the tray for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven to 150°C fan.
Using a serrated knife, cut each log diagonally into slices about 1 cm thick. Lay the slices flat on the lined tray.

Bake at 150°C fan for 15 to 20 minutes, turning each biscotto once halfway through, until completely dry and crisp on both sides. They will harden further as they cool. Store in an airtight tin immediately once cooled.

attrs.problem: Log crumbles when sliced after the first bake
attrs.avoid: Avoid slicing too soon; the log must be cool enough to handle firmly.
attrs.fix: Leave the log to cool for at least 20 minutes. A very sharp serrated knife, using a sawing motion rather than pressing down, prevents crumbling.

attrs.problem: Biscotti still slightly soft after the second bake
attrs.avoid: Avoid removing from the oven before they feel completely rigid to the touch.
attrs.fix: Return for a further 5 minutes. They should sound hollow when tapped and bend without give.
